frequency_question: How often do substantive monetary policy easing cycles successfully satisfy formal threshold and announcement criteria within a defined window?
membership_rule: Includes all official scheduled and unscheduled policy rate decisions by the central bank during the time window; excludes non-rate policy tools like QE or reserve requirement changes unless accompanied by a rate cut meeting the exact basis point threshold.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 major easing cycles examined; all successfully met the numerical and formal statement criteria when rate cuts occurred.
known_gaps: None of significance; standard FOMC procedures ensure any rate cut is officially announced in a statement.
skeleton: 4 major easing cycles since 2000, each containing multiple meetings where at least one rate cut of >=25 bps occurred successfully within the window.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 applicable easing decision windows where the substantive intent was present
validity_reason: Central bank communication and rate-setting mechanisms remain structurally consistent over multi-year horizons.
